[
  {
    "title": "Bulk discount misses exactly ten units",
    "desc": "The plan grants 5% off at 10 or more units, but this branch uses `qty > 10`, so a quantity of exactly 10 receives no bulk discount. This also affects invoice totals because the renderer calls `line_total` for each row.",
    "importance": "high",
    "file": "shop/pricing.py",
    "line_range": [31, 31],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "elif qty > 10:",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan explicitly sets the 5% threshold at 10 units.",
    "scope_reference": "Pricing rules: Bulk discount",
    ""
  },
  {
    "title": "Customers without a tier raise KeyError",
    "desc": "The plan says a customer whose tier is `None` pays list price, but this lookup has no entry for `None` and raises `KeyError`. Consequently, `line_total` and invoice rendering fail for customers without a tier.",
    "importance": "high",
    "file": "shop/pricing.py",
    "line_range": [42, 42],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "return TIER_RATES[customer.tier]",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan requires customers without a tier to pay list price.",
    "scope_reference": "Pricing rules: Customer tier",
    "scope_reference": "Pricing rules: Customer tier"
  },
  {
    "title": "Line totals use floats and banker rounding",
    "desc": "This converts prices and discount factors to floats, then uses Python's `round`, which uses ties-to-even rather than the required `ROUND_HALF_UP`. For example, a gold customer's 0.50 item with quantity 1 yields an exact discounted amount of 0.485, which should round to 0.49 but can round to 0.48 here; the float arithmetic also violates the plan's Decimal-only requirement.",
    "importance": "high",
    "file": "shop/pricing.py",
    "line_range": [49, 50],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "amount = float(itm.price) * qty",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan requires Decimal arithmetic and per-line ROUND_HALF_UP rounding.",
    "scope_reference": "Pricing rules: Money"
  },
  {
    "title": "Coupon expiry check is reversed",
    "desc": "The plan rejects a coupon when `expires_at` is before `now`, but this condition raises for a coupon whose expiry is after `now`. Expired coupons are therefore accepted, while still-valid coupons are rejected.",
    "importance": "high",
    "file": "shop/pricing.py",
    "line_range": [55, 55],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "if coupon.expires_at > now:",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan specifies rejection only when expiry is before the current time.",
    "scope_reference": "Coupons"
  },
  {
    "title": "Releasing stock increases reservations",
    "desc": "Releasing a reservation should subtract the released quantity, but this adds it to the reserved count. After reserving 3 units and releasing 1, the reservation becomes 4 instead of 2, reducing available stock further and potentially preventing other carts from reserving it.",
    "importance": "high",
    "file": "shop/stock.py",
    "line_range": [37, 37],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "self.reserved.get(sku, 0) + qty",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan requires release to take the quantity off the reserved count.",
    "scope_reference": "Stock reservation"
  },
  {
    "title": "Long SKUs break invoice column alignment",
    "desc": "The invoice formats the SKU with a minimum width of eight characters but does not truncate it, so longer SKUs shift the item, quantity, and total columns. The neighboring item-name field is explicitly truncated, indicating the renderer is intended to preserve its fixed-width row layout.",
    "importance": "medium",
    "file": "shop/invoice.py",
    "line_range": [29, 29],
    "type": "bug",
    "anchor_text": "{item.sku:<8}{name:<28}",
    "scope_relation": "in_scope",
    "scope_reason": "The plan requires invoice lines to render as fixed-width text.",
    "scope_reference": "Invoice text"
  }
]
